title: The Edge Case Solved Database — Solved: Empty String Input to Text Pipeline
body: Public edition. Public knowledge, fact-checked reference. Resolution: Solved: Empty String Input to Text Pipeline. Root cause: String.prototype.split on "" returns [""] by spec: splitting an empty string still yields one (empty) segment. Code that assumed "split gives tokens" inherited a phantom token. Fix: Guard at the pipeline entry: if input.trim() is empty, return [] before splitting. Tokenize only non-empty input. Verification: 1) Run tokenize("") and tokenize("a b"). 2) Assert [] and ["a","b"] respectively. 3) Assert no phantom token reaches downstream. title: The Edge Case Solved Database — Solved: Aggregation Over an Empty Array
body: Public edition. Public knowledge, fact-checked reference. Resolution: Solved: Aggregation Over an Empty Array. Root cause: sum/length with length 0 computes 0/0 = NaN. NaN then fails every comparison silently (NaN !== NaN), so the bad value is never caught downstream. Fix: Return an explicit empty signal: if the array is empty, return null (or {empty:true}) instead of dividing. Callers branch on the signal. title: The Edge Case Solved Database — Solved: Integer Precision Loss Beyond 2^53
body: Public edition. Public knowledge, fact-checked reference. Resolution: Solved: Integer Precision Loss Beyond 2^53. Root cause: JavaScript numbers are 64-bit floats; integers above 2^53 cannot all be represented, so n+1 === n+2. Quadrillion-scale ordinals stored as Number collide. Fix: Use BigInt for all generator counters and ID ordinals at or beyond 2^53. Serialize BigInt as strings (JSON-safe) and parse back with BigInt(). Verification: 1) BigInt(2)^53n+1n !== 2^53n+2n. 2) String round-trip preserves the value. 3) Assert distinct ordinals stay distinct. How to run: save the fix program as fix.js and run: node fix.js. title: The Edge Case Solved Database — Solved: Catastrophic Regex Backtracking
body: Public edition. Public knowledge, fact-checked reference. Resolution: Solved: Catastrophic Regex Backtracking. title: The Edge Case Solved Database — Solved: Negative Zero Ambiguity
body: Public edition. Public knowledge, fact-checked reference. Resolution: Solved: Negative Zero Ambiguity. title: The Edge Case Solved Database — Solved: Duplicate Keys in JSON Parse
body: Public edition. Public knowledge, fact-checked reference. Resolution: Solved: Duplicate Keys in JSON Parse. Root cause: JSON.parse follows the spec: later duplicate keys overwrite earlier ones with no signal. Merged configs and hand-written payloads lose values invisibly. Fix: Parse with a strict JSON reader that tracks keys per object and throws on the first duplicate instead of silently overwriting.
